chapter: National Guard band and first jobs in Chicago
title: Bobby Williams, the trumpeter who sounded like Roy Eldridge
summary: After Dolly left they used a young trumpeter and a Louisville drummer; Caldwell praises Bobby Williams of the Sunset and the way older players encouraged youngsters.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: She had the group, and then when she left, then we turned it over, had a fellow named Wilson, was a very good trumpet player, young fellow. We all was young. Then we got a drummer from Louisville named Burton because Bobby Williams was working with -- with the -- at the Sunset with Cat Correll Dickerson, with -- beautiful trumpet player. Bobby, his name was in that book, but when you ever heard him play, Roy Eldridge (unintelligible) was just a replica of what Bobby Williams was.
Oh, that's interesting. (Unintelligible). I mean this was very early, isn't it? he was a
Yeah, but (unintelligible) wonderful trumpet player, always execution.

He got with the -- funny thing about that, I think he ate something with poison that sit back on him. He was a fine fellow, very fine fellow. Only, you know, thing about those fellows, when we were kids, young guys coming up, they always liked to see us make progress. They say, when you got to the folks you can play something. Well, what do you want to play? We say, oh, we play so and so, so (Simon and and so. All right. We go in there, sit in and play, myself and Cecil Irwin.
